attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the comparison in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the tentative comparison and retrospective scope. Its wording retains the hedge despite the categorical modality field.

contract.note: The contract converts a tentative impression into a majority threshold. The plain-reading provision cannot make hedged language scorable, and significant ROI and any measurable productivity value are not equivalent.

evidence.note: The vendor-published survey reports only 23% seeing significant agent ROI within the target period. It supports limited significant returns, although the excerpt does not establish an agent-adopter-only denominator.
The contemporaneous analyst assessment supports limited value and substantial hype. Its separate cancellation forecast does not establish an observed outcome.

The survey fits the contract's measurable-value branch and provides relevant counterevidence. However, reported productivity gains do not measure ROI after investment costs and cannot directly contradict limited significant ROI.

The selected early-adopter population and unclear attribution of returns to agents versus generative AI do not establish broad agent ROI. The summary also contains inconsistent release and fieldwork chronology.

reviews.rationale: Marcus offers a hedged assessment of agents to date. Policy excludes such tentative language from scoring, and the contract cannot remove that hedge through a plain-reading interpretation. The evidence also uses materially different thresholds for significant ROI and productivity value.
